source.title: Resting Neurons, Active Insights: Robustifying Activation Sparsity in LLMs via Spontaneity
source.authors: Haotian Xu; Jian-Nan Yang; Tian Gao; T. Weng; Teng-Fei Ma

record.file_problem: The full paper, including appendices, is present. Some figure text and tables are garbled in the extraction, but the relevant representation-analysis results are also described in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures how activation sparsification changes representations within a model and whether SPON reduces that shift. It does not test convergence among independently trained models, cross-modal alignment, representation mapping, recurring features, or metric/data dependence as defined in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The representation results compare dense models with their activation-sparse counterparts, rather than independent models converging as scale or capability increases. The paper reports CKA and latent-space deviation results; these are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version, not as tests of a listed version. Other performance, sparsity, latency, and pruning results do not measure the claim's alignment behavior.
record.test_reason: The study compares each LLM's activation-sparse variants (TEAL, SPON) with that same model's dense counterpart using CKA and t-SNE l2 deviation. No independently trained models, seeds, modalities, cross-model maps or recurring features are compared, so no version is tested. The paper uses 'representational alignment' to mean sparse-to-dense fidelity within one model, a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that activation sparsity causes representational drift from the dense model, and that SPON reduces this drift (higher CKA, lower latent shift), which they say explains its better accuracy retention. They frame the drift reduction as substantial, although the l2 reductions are about 4–8%.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation sparsification and learned input-independent activation vectors, then compares sparse and dense representations using CKA and latent-space deviation. It does not reproduce the original studies' independent-model similarity measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Against each model's dense counterpart, SPON-sparse models show higher layerwise CKA than TEAL-sparse models (Llama3-8B, shown in a figure). They also show lower t-SNE l2 shift: Llama3-8B 8.69→8.21, Mistral-7B 13.33→12.82, Qwen3-8B 6.76→6.24, all at 50% sparsity on 50 WikiText prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned input-independent activation offsets partly preserve a model's dense hidden representations under 50% activation sparsity, compared with magnitude thresholding alone.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The representation analysis is limited to comparisons with each model's dense counterpart; it does not examine independently trained models. The text provides only a qualitative CKA comparison, and the reported latent deviation is based on 50 prompts. No uncertainty estimates are stated for these representation results.
record.rows_left_out: No additional representation-alignment results were left out. Other task accuracy, efficiency, pruning, and sparsity results do not measure the claim's listed alignment behaviors.

untested.parts: All of V1: no comparison of independently trained models across scale or capability.
All of V2: no vision-language paired-data alignment.
All of V3: no networks of the same architecture trained from different seeds.
All of V4: no mapping or stitching between different models.
All of V5: no recurring features or circuits across models.
All of V6: CKA is used only for sparse-vs-dense comparison, with no metric or input variation for cross-model convergence.
All of V7: no cross-model alignment levels and no causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses classification is confirmed. CKA here is a within-model fidelity diagnostic for the study's own method, which is closer to T4-style use. No version is tested. No uncertainty is reported for the representation results.

versions.untested_parts: Independent models with varying architectures, objectives, data, scale, and capability.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions as model capability changes.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized networks of the same architecture.
Mapping representations between models, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.

Whether convergence changes across similarity metrics, settings, or input distributions. CKA and latent-space deviation are used for sparse-versus-dense comparisons, not as a test of metric dependence in convergence.
Whether partial alignment across independently trained models is explained by shared training data or objectives.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured average latent-space deviation from the dense model for the activation-sparse TEAL model.
rows.note: The paper reports this as deviation from the dense counterpart; it is not a comparison of independently trained models.
rows.check: This is a t-SNE-space l2 shift from the model's own dense version, on 50 prompts. It is a study-method comparison (TEAL vs SPON), not convergence.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured average latent-space deviation from the dense model for the activation-sparse model with SPON.
rows.note: The paper states this is lower than the TEAL result for the same backbone.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B
rows.operation_detail: Measured average latent-space deviation from the dense model for the activation-sparse TEAL model.
rows.note: Figure 13 reports this deviation for the TEAL comparison; it is a sparse-versus-dense comparison within one model family.

rows.subject: Mistral-7B

rows.note: Figure 13 reports this deviation for the SPON comparison.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared layerwise CKA between dense and activation-sparse representations.
rows.measure: Layerwise CKA similarity to dense model
rows.value: TEAL has lower layerwise CKA similarity than SPON; no aggregate scalar stated
rows.note: The paper describes the TEAL comparison as losing resemblance to the dense baseline; layerwise values are shown in the CKA figure.
rows.check: The value is qualitative. The Figure 6/12 heatmaps give layerwise numbers (e.g. TEAL diagonal roughly 0.3–0.9), but the extraction is garbled. This is a within-model sparse-vs-dense comparison, not cross-model.

rows.subject: Llama3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared layerwise CKA between dense and activation-sparse representations.
rows.measure: Layerwise CKA similarity to dense model
rows.value: SPON has consistently higher layerwise CKA similarity than TEAL; Appendix F says diagonal entries exceed 95% similarity
rows.note: This evaluates preservation of a model's own dense representations after sparsification, not cross-model convergence.
rows.check: The '>95% diagonal' figure is the authors' wording. The garbled heatmap shows SPON diagonal values around 0.87–0.97 in many layers and lower in the final layers, so 'over 95%' looks overstated. Not a cross-model comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
